patch_description: Keep the direct-demand linear reward, and add only demand-conditioned two-hop interactions. A path \(i \to j \to k\) is rewarded only when \(t[i,k] > 0\), with its reward scaled by how strongly demand supports the incoming and outgoing legs at the intermediate node. The normalized inbound/outbound shares make the profile comparable across nodes and prevent generic two-hop paths from receiving the same reward. The interaction set is at most \(n(n-1)(n-2)\), within the term limit, and avoids the broader shared-endpoint and reciprocal-link penalties that performed worse.
